description: STAGE-CONSISTENCY BASELINE for saga #811 (issue #816 item 5): the `check()` half of a pair whose `-execute` sibling WAS a characterization fixture and is now a `REGRESSION WALL` — issue #815 flipped it, and no characterization fixture remains in the corpus. This half did not move, which is what the pair exists to show: the fix changed the run and left the check alone. This half was ALREADY CORRECT before the fix and survived it UNCHANGED — it was precisely the answer the run path never consulted, which is the whole of saga #811's shape-A mechanism. Fault shape A — an UNRESOLVABLE NAME in argument position. `check()` computes the right answer (`ol-unknown-command`, whose usual stage is `semantic` per spec/error-model.md:97). At the time this fixture was written `execute()` never consulted it, so the statement was discarded whole with no diagnostic and no effect; measured after issue #815, the same program reports that diagnostic and emits zero events — this half is unchanged either way, which is the point of a stage-consistency baseline. `forward` is resolvable here because `turtle-rendering` is in this fixture's active profile set, so the only diagnostic is the real one on `wibble` — the same source under `core-language` alone would additionally flag `forward` itself, which is the false positive `profile-argument/` pins.
